title: Add a safe board sync command (kbs sync)
description:
Problem: the board lives in git and each checkout/worktree sees only its own copy. Comments added in another clone are invisible until pulled. Observed 2026-10-12/13 in the Papyrus repo: the primary checkout was 16 commits behind, and git pull --ff-only aborted because kbs had dirtied board files. Agents and sessions hand-merged the board from a clean clone three times using a three-way merge.

Evidence not verified here: the Papyrus incidents (reported by Ryan). Verified: kbs 0.32.0 has no sync command (kbs --help lists none; kbs commit only stages project/issues/ per AGENTS.md).

Acceptance:
- One command (kbs sync or similar) that fetches the shared board branch, three-way merges board files (append-only event files unioned; issue JSON merged per field), commits and pushes.
- Idempotent: running twice is a no-op the second time.
- Safe: never touches non-board files; refuses with a clear message instead of overwriting uncommitted non-board changes; a dirty board working tree does not abort it.
- Has a --dry-run that reports what would merge.
- Gherkin scenario covering a comment added in a second clone appearing after sync.
right_now_summary: A safe `kbs sync` command is needed to merge and push board changes across clones without touching other files.
